title: New Year in Paris 2027: fireworks, access and what opens on 1 January
description: Plan New Year in Paris 2027: Champs-Élysées celebrations, Arc de Triomphe early closing, a daytime Tuileries walk and transport details still pending.
intro: To welcome 2027 in Paris, the tourist office’s published programme focuses on the Champs-Élysées and Arc de Triomphe: a free evening on 31 December 2026, with access announced from 7 pm, a projection on the monument and fireworks at midnight. Entering the Arc is a separate activity: its operator announces an early 4 pm closure that day. This guide separates the two experiences and adds the Tuileries as a daytime walk, without turning the garden into a night-time viewing location.

There is an important qualification in the information checked on 12 November 2026. Although the tourism calendar already describes precise transport arrangements, RATP still asks readers to return in December for its new programme. Free travel, all-night lines and station reopening times are therefore not treated here as confirmed for 2026–2027. Plan around the announced event, then finalise logistics using the operator’s and authorities’ latest notices.

quickFacts.label: Announced celebration
quickFacts.value: 31 December 2026 on the Champs-Élysées; public access announced from 7 pm

quickFacts.label: Show
quickFacts.value: Projection announced 11:50 pm; midnight fireworks at the Arc

quickFacts.label: Monument visit
quickFacts.value: Arc closes 4 pm on 31 December; no midnight terrace admission included

quickFacts.label: New Year’s Day
quickFacts.value: Louvre Museum closed; Tuileries Garden access is separate

sections.heading: Champs-Élysées: choose the public celebration and plan entry
paragraphs: The avenue is the gathering place announced by Paris je t’aime for 31 December 2026. It is an outdoor, free event, with public access planned from 7 pm and entrance checks. The published information identifies Concorde as the main entrance and names other side approaches, but that does not guarantee any particular street will be open on arrival. Consult final maps and instructions, especially if your accommodation sits inside or beside the celebration perimeter.

Treat arrival as part of the event: decide who you will enter with, agree how to regroup if separated, and consider whether staying to the end suits everyone’s mobility. The daytime archive photograph looks along the avenue from the Arc de Triomphe in 2009, rather than recording 2026 decorations, capacity or entry points. A daytime visit can help you orient yourself, but it still cannot guarantee the same route will remain available after the night-time event arrangements are installed.

sections.heading: Arc de Triomphe: daytime monument, evening backdrop
paragraphs: The Arc plays two different roles in this break. As a monument, it offers an individually ticketed visit; as a façade, it is the focus of the projection announced for the change of year. The Centre des monuments nationaux publishes early closure at 4 pm on 31 December 2026, with last admission 45 minutes before closing. General winter evening hours do not override that exception. If you want to ascend, reserve a daytime admission product and slot that respect the early closure.

For the evening, the tourist office announces projection from 11:50 pm and fireworks at midnight. That gives no access to the terrace, interior or every area immediately beneath the monument. Nor does it establish a guaranteed sightline from a particular position among the crowd. The archive photograph shows the illuminated Arc in 2024 without the 2026 performance. When choosing between an ascent and the celebration, treat each as a distinct experience with its own conditions and timing.

sections.heading: Tuileries: a winter walk rather than a midnight waiting place
paragraphs: The Tuileries Garden provides a daytime block in the same part of Paris. Its operator, the Louvre, publishes free admission throughout the year and winter opening from 7:30 am to 7:30 pm in November, December and January, among other months. Visitors are asked to leave 30 minutes before closure. Those arrangements must not be interpreted as permission to wait for fireworks inside the garden or a guarantee against exceptional security closures.

For 1 January, distinguish the garden from the museum: the Louvre closes its galleries on that holiday and lists outdoor access separately. Check notices for the day before approaching. A short walk beside the pond and along the garden axes can work after a long evening, with breaks and without another demanding reservation immediately afterwards. The Ferris wheel in the photograph belongs to a 2011 image; it does not establish a current installation, an open attraction or a 2026–2027 festive programme.

sections.heading: The announced programme for welcoming 2027
paragraphs: Both official tourism pages are dated for 31 December 2026 and the arrival of 2027. They describe an evening on the avenue, projection on the Arc façade, a countdown and midnight fireworks. That is the basis of this plan. A photograph from another year is not used as documentation of the future show, and the Eiffel Tower is not assigned a celebration that these sources place on the Arc and Champs-Élysées axis.

The published programme remains subject to operational instructions issued nearer the date and exceptional changes. Before setting out, check whether the event is maintained and how access is organised. If you prefer a dinner, cruise or indoor party, verify its meeting point, duration, inclusions and departure arrangements. A private activity advertised as a réveillon does not guarantee admission to the avenue or a view of the Arc show. Choose the experience you actually want before comparing products.

sections.heading: Transport: RATP’s new plan still needs updating
paragraphs: In the current capture, RATP says the previous festive period is over and asks readers to return in December 2026 for a new programme. The page retains a January 2026 modification date. That prevents a line list, free-travel period or station schedule from being treated as confirmation for the coming night when it is not yet supplied by the operator, even if a tourism page already reproduces it. This does not establish that transport will be absent; it means this check did not verify the specific 2026–2027 plan.

Once published, review the outward route, the return journey and the stations actually served, rather than only the line name. Keep an alternative walk to an available departure point after the event, suited to your mobility and accommodation location. Enter the holiday date into the planner for 1 January too, allowing a buffer for any rail or flight connection. Returning to the hotel after midnight and departing early can be incompatible with a lengthy sightseeing visit the following morning.

sections.heading: Admissions, checks and meals: keep bookings compatible
paragraphs: Separate the costs: the announced outdoor gathering is free, while monument admission, dinner and a private show are different purchases. For the Arc, check available slots, entry conditions and the special 4 pm closure. Do not buy an ascent expecting to remain on the terrace until the countdown. The operator warns that ceremonies or weather can cause exceptional closure, so reviewing its notices remains worthwhile even when you hold a ticket.

The tourist office describes security checks and restrictions on items such as glass and alcohol, and discourages pushchairs in the gathering. Prepare your evening bag according to the final rules without adding bulky belongings that make entry difficult. Arrange a meal before entering the perimeter or book an option whose timing genuinely fits the celebration. Do not assume a usual terrace or shop will remain available at midnight, or that leaving to eat will let you recover the same position in the audience.

itinerary: 30 December or the day before your main evening: if you want to enter the Arc, select an available slot and check that day’s exceptions. A daytime walk along part of the avenue helps with orientation, while event entrances remain separate information to check. Leave room for a meal and an unhurried return to your accommodation.

31 December: a short daytime activity or a rest, preparation, then travel towards the entrance identified in final notices. Public access to the avenue is announced from 7 pm, projection from 11:50 pm and fireworks at midnight. Those timings do not guarantee late arrival will be possible or that the Arc interior remains open.

1 January: a later breakfast and a daytime Tuileries walk if access is operating, without trying to enter the Louvre’s closed galleries. If the weather is unsuitable, choose an activity whose holiday calendar you have verified. The general Paris guide linked below helps fill other days without making every attraction compulsory on New Year’s Day.

faq.question: Where are the Paris 2027 New Year fireworks announced?
faq.answer: Paris je t’aime places the show on the Champs-Élysées and Arc de Triomphe façade axis for 31 December 2026. It announces projection from 11:50 pm and fireworks at midnight. Check the final programme before travelling.

faq.question: Do I need Arc admission for the avenue celebration?
faq.answer: These are separate access arrangements. The outdoor evening is announced as free; the monument has its own ticket and closes early at 4 pm on 31 December 2026. That ticket does not provide a midnight terrace visit.

faq.question: Is free transport throughout the night confirmed?
faq.answer: A final 2026–2027 RATP plan was not verified. The operator page still asks readers to return in December 2026. Check its update before relying on free travel, times and station reopenings from another edition.

faq.question: Can I visit the Louvre on 1 January 2027?
faq.answer: The Louvre Museum closes on 1 January. Tuileries access is listed separately under daytime winter hours, subject to notices and exceptional changes. The garden is not an all-night enclosure for waiting until midnight.

conclusion: A well-planned Paris New Year separates the outdoor show, a daytime Arc visit and the pace of 1 January. The published programme provides a specific date and focus; transport and final entrances require a last check. Compatible reservations and honestly labelled archive photographs help you plan without confusing cultural admission with a guaranteed position in front of the fireworks.
